references.text: The preceding verse ([ref:Joh 4:23|John 4:23]) introduces the statement that God is spirit and that those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth. Verse 24 provides the theological basis for what Jesus says in verse 23 about true worshippers.

[ref:2 Kor 3:17|2 Corinthians 3:17] states, "The Lord is the Spirit," and where the Lord's Spirit is, there is freedom. Paul links the liberating work of the Spirit to the ministry of the new covenant, which illuminates the spiritual worship Jesus describes in contrast to external forms.
[ref:Rom 12:1|Romans 12:1] speaks of presenting ourselves as a living sacrifice, a "spiritual act of worship" (λογικὴν λατρείαν), expressing the spiritual worship Jesus refers to.
[ref:Fil 3:3|Philippians 3:3] says that we who worship by God's Spirit (πνεύματι θεοῦ λατρεύοντες) are the true circumcision – worship in the Spirit as opposed to external ceremony.
[ref:Joh 1:18|John 1:18] affirms that no one has seen God, emphasizing God's spiritual and invisible nature and thus the need for spiritual worship.
[ref:Joh 1:14|John 1:14] describes Jesus as "full of grace and truth." The truth (ἀλήθεια) that characterizes right worship in John 4:24 is linked to Jesus' revelation.
[ref:Joh 14:6|John 14:6] – Jesus says, "I am the way, the truth, and the life." Worship "in truth" is connected with worshipping through him who is the very truth.
[ref:Joh 14:17|John 14:17] refers to the Holy Spirit as the "Spirit of truth," uniting the two aspects of worship – "in spirit and truth."
[ref:Joh 3:5-6|John 3:5-6] distinguishes between what is born of flesh and what is born of the Spirit. That God is spirit means that approaching him occurs through the new birth of the Spirit.
[ref:1 Joh 5:6|1 John 5:6] says that "the Spirit is the truth," linking spirit and truth in the same way John 4:24 does in connection with worship.
[ref:Jes 31:3|Isaiah 31:3] contrasts flesh and spirit: "The Egyptians are men and not God, their horses are flesh and not spirit." This underscores God's spiritual nature in contrast to the earthly.
[ref:5 Mos 4:15-16|Deuteronomy 4:15-16] warns against making any image of God because the people saw no form – God is spirit and cannot be reduced to external forms.
[ref:Sal 145:18|Psalm 145:18] says that the Lord is near all who call on him "in truth," reflecting the requirement to worship in truth.
[ref:1 Tim 1:17|1 Timothy 1:17] praises God as eternal, immortal, and invisible – qualities consistent with God being spirit and therefore requiring worship in spirit and truth.
[ref:Kol 1:15|Colossians 1:15] calls Christ "the image of the invisible God." That God is an invisible spirit is why he reveals himself in the Son – and is worshipped through him.
